descriptions.description: The American College of Radiology Imaging Network (ACRIN) trial 6698 was a multi-center study to evaluate the effectiveness of quantitative diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) for assessing breast cancer response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). ACRIN 6698 was performed as a sub-study of the ongoing I-SPY 2 TRIAL (Investigation of Serial studies to Predict Your Therapeutic Response with Imaging And moLecular Analysis 2), an adaptive, multi-agent phase II trial designed to quickly identify new agents for breast cancer. This collection includes serial MRI studies with DWI, DCE and T2w acquisitions on women undergoing NAC for invasive breast cancer, with single-visit test/retest DWI acquisitions on a subset of the trial subjects.
